title: Triage I: START & JumpSTART
learningObjectives: Triage an adult with START in under 60 seconds (goal ~30 s).
Triage a child with JumpSTART, including the 5-rescue-breath rule.
Use only the lifesaving interventions START allows during triage.
Recognize when START criteria mislead (cold, dark, walkers who are sick).

summary.title: START in One Breath
summary.content: Simple Triage And Rapid Treatment uses three physiological checks — RPM: Respirations, Perfusion, Mental status. Step 0: everyone who can WALK → MINOR (green). Then for each non-walker: Breathing? If no → open/position airway → starts breathing = IMMEDIATE (red); still apneic = DECEASED (black). Breathing > 30/min = IMMEDIATE. Perfusion: radial pulse absent OR capillary refill > 2 s = IMMEDIATE (control bleeding). Mental status: can't follow simple commands = IMMEDIATE. Passed everything = DELAYED (yellow).

summary.title: What You May Do During START
summary.content: Only two things, both seconds long: open the airway (position it; insert an airway adjunct if instantly available per protocol) and control major bleeding (direct pressure/tourniquet — or have a green patient hold pressure). Then tag and move. No CPR, no splinting, no oxygen, no IVs during primary triage. Target: ~30 seconds per patient, never more than 60.

summary.title: JumpSTART for Kids (≈1–8 years)
summary.content: Children arrest from hypoxia, and normal pediatric vitals differ — so JumpSTART adapts START. Walk → MINOR. Not breathing → position airway → breathing = IMMEDIATE; still apneic → check PERIPHERAL PULSE: none = DECEASED; pulse present → give 5 RESCUE BREATHS (~15 s) → breathing = IMMEDIATE, still apneic = DECEASED. Breathing: RR < 15 or > 45 = IMMEDIATE. Perfusion: no palpable peripheral pulse = IMMEDIATE. Mental status (AVPU): 'P' with inappropriate response (non-localizing, posturing) or 'U' = IMMEDIATE; A, V, or appropriate P = DELAYED. If the patient looks like a child → JumpSTART; looks like a young adult → START.

summary.title: Babies and Kids Who Can't Walk Yet
summary.content: Infants and toddlers who are not developmentally able to walk go straight through the JumpSTART algorithm (they can't 'pass' the walk test). Per JumpSTART guidance, a well-appearing non-walker with normal JumpSTART findings and no significant external injury may be tagged MINOR; otherwise DELAYED or IMMEDIATE by the criteria. A child carried out by a parent is triaged as an individual — not automatically green.

summary.title: Where START Fools You
summary.content: Capillary refill is unreliable in the cold and dark → use the radial pulse. Walkers can be sick (internal bleeding, chest pain, pregnancy, blast lung, toxic exposures with delayed onset) — they're green for sorting, not for life: re-triage them. START is a snapshot: a yellow with a pelvic fracture can be red in 20 minutes. Over-triaging everyone to red feels safe but buries the true reds and raises their mortality.

clinicalPearls: RPM = 30-2-Can do: RR > 30 → red; CRT > 2 s (or no radial) → red; can't follow commands → red.
In START an RR of exactly 30 does NOT trigger red — the cutoff is MORE than 30.
JumpSTART numbers: 15–45 is 'OK'; outside that range is red.
Kids get a pulse check and 5 rescue breaths before being tagged deceased — the only 'resuscitation' in mass triage.
Use green patients as helpers: 'Hold pressure here, don't let go until someone relieves you.'
redFlags: Spending > 60 seconds per patient — the triage line stops.
Starting CPR on an apneic adult during START.
Tagging a child deceased without the pulse check / 5 breaths step.
Relying on capillary refill in a cold night-time scene.
commonMistakes: Using adult START cut-offs on a toddler (RR 40 is normal for a 2-year-old).
Treating 'walking' as 'uninjured' — greens still need assessment and re-triage.
Forgetting to open the airway before tagging an apneic adult deceased.
memoryAids: Black needs TWO things in a child: no breathing after positioning AND (no pulse OR no breathing after 5 breaths).

decisionTrees.title: START (Adult)
decisionTrees.content:
Can walk? → YES: MINOR (green)
  NO ↓
Breathing?
  → NO: position airway → breathing? YES: IMMEDIATE | NO: DECEASED
  → YES ↓
RR > 30? → YES: IMMEDIATE
  NO ↓
Radial pulse absent OR CRT > 2 s? → YES: IMMEDIATE (control bleeding)
  NO ↓
Follows simple commands? → NO: IMMEDIATE | YES: DELAYED

decisionTrees.title: JumpSTART (Child ~1–8 y)
decisionTrees.content:
Can walk? → YES: MINOR
  NO ↓
Breathing?
  → NO: position airway → breathing? YES: IMMEDIATE
        NO → palpable peripheral pulse? NO: DECEASED
                YES → 5 rescue breaths → breathing? YES: IMMEDIATE | NO: DECEASED
  → YES ↓
RR < 15 or > 45? → YES: IMMEDIATE
  NO ↓
Palpable peripheral pulse? → NO: IMMEDIATE
  YES ↓
AVPU: U or inappropriate P → IMMEDIATE | A, V, appropriate P → DELAYED
